title: The mutational dynamics of the Arabidopsis centromeres.

verified.what_i_actually_checked: Europe PMC: not open access, no PMCID, no supplement, no text-mined accessions, no NCBI links. Zenodo search on the topic found nothing for this paper. Listed the full GitHub code repository tree: shell/Python/C++ scripts plus a data/ folder holding only reference files (CEN1 sequence, CEN178 repeat positions, consensus repeat FASTA); no per-mutation table. ENA analysis-file query for PRJEB112076 returned an empty listing. Nature article page redirects to a login.
verified.what_came_from_paper_text_only: From the bioRxiv preprint (v2) text: 8 MA32 mutation accumulation lines (256 generations) yielding 208 centromeric point mutations, 56 large indels (insertion-deletions over 50 bp) and 6 small indels (270 total); 5 HPG1 natural lines with 1,113 point mutations, 275 large and 27 small indels; 3 rtel1-1 mutant lines; assemblies deposited under PRJNA1259971, PRJEB112076, PRJEB75768, PRJNA1458610; per-mutation lists said to be in Supplementary Tables 11-14, which I could not retrieve.

a1_downloadable.note: Genome assemblies are said to be in public NCBI/ENA BioProjects and code is on GitHub (verified); the per-mutation supplementary tables sit with the paywalled Nature article and were not retrieved.

a2_label_is_a_column.note: The only labelled unit is a mutation call; a usable label (e.g. mutated vs unmutated repeat unit) would have to be built by aligning replicated whole-genome assemblies with the authors' pipeline. Checked GitHub: no mutation table is shipped.

a3_inputs_present.note: Centromere sequences would be available from the deposited assemblies (paper text) and a CEN1 sequence file is in the GitHub repo (verified).

a4_units_stated.note: Mutation types and positions in base pairs; not an issue for this data type (paper text).

a5_enough_rows.note: Preprint reports 270 centromeric mutations in 8 MA lines (plus about 1,415 in 5 natural HPG1 lines, of a different kind: divergence, not controlled accumulation). Under the ~1,500-row bar and far too few positive events for per-site prediction; not verified in files.

a6_fits_laptop.working_set: Five centromeres of ~2-3 Mb each per assembly; well under 1 GB.
a6_fits_laptop.note: Size is not the problem (estimate from genome size).

a7_counts_match_paper.note: Could not compare: supplementary mutation tables not retrievable and no mutation file in the code repository.

a8_label_provenance.note: Mutations are measured by comparing independent replicated long-read assemblies, a physical measurement rather than a model output (paper text).

backbone.name: A DNA language model such as Nucleotide Transformer could embed repeat units, but there is too little label to fit a head.

integration.partner_dataset: 1001 Genomes long-read centromere assemblies of natural Arabidopsis accessions
integration.join_key: centromere coordinates / CEN178 repeat unit alignment
integration.bigger_question_one_sentence: Does the mutation spectrum measured in the lab explain the centromere diversity seen across natural accessions? — a population-genetics simulation question, not an ML one.

honest_claim_h3: With 270 mutations in 8 lines, a model could at best describe where in a centromere mutations happened in these lines; it could not predict mutation risk per site with any confidence.

plain_idea.one_liner: Use the DNA sequence around each centromeric repeat unit to predict whether it gains a point mutation or an insertion/deletion over generations.
plain_idea.train_on: Repeat units (about 178 bp each) from Arabidopsis centromere assemblies with their sequence context; only 270 mutation events in 8 lab lines reported (paper text, not verified).
plain_idea.predict: Whether a repeat unit was mutated, with truth from comparing replicated long-read genome assemblies of lines propagated for 256 generations.
plain_idea.why_worthwhile: Centromere biologists would learn which sequence features make repeat arrays mutable; but the event count is too small for a model to add beyond the paper's descriptive statistics.

ml_idea: Per-repeat-unit mutability classifier on centromere sequence context; rejected because only ~270 mutation events exist and labels must be rebuilt from assembly alignments.

effort.compute_note: Estimated only: rebuilding mutation calls means running the authors' assembly-comparison pipeline on ~20 assemblies; nothing was timed.
effort.cheapest_killing_check: Count mutation events in Supplementary Tables 11-14: preprint already says 270 in the MA lines, which kills it.

verdict_reason: Fails A5 and A2: preprint reports only 270 centromeric mutations across 8 mutation accumulation lines, no mutation table is in the public code repository (checked), and labels would have to be rebuilt by aligning genome assemblies. A discovery paper, not an ML dataset.
